reason: The hypothesis combines the idea of controlled annealing to precipitate nanoscale intermetallics (from P1 and P11) with the role of Ti-rich films in corrosion passivation (from P3) and the formation of protective Al-rich oxide scales (from P23, P26) into a single mechanism linking thermal treatment to simultaneous improvements in both high-temperature oxidation and aqueous corrosion. None of the passages proposes this specific dual-property improvement via a single annealing step, nor do they link the precipitation of intermetallics to the subsequent surface partitioning of reactive elements for oxide scale formation. This represents a synthesis of findings from multiple papers into a new proposal.

uniformly dispersed nanoscale intermetallics improve properties (P11)

Al and Cr form protective oxide scales at high temperatures (P23, P26)
reducing micro-galvanic corrosion by refining intermetallic distribution (P10)
